## Summary of Changes

The bug was in **Aegis Password Manager** — during first-time setup (and the later "set password" dialog), checking "show password" caused the password confirmation field to be **disabled**, which cleared its text. The validation logic then saw an empty confirm field but returned `true` due to the `|| isChecked` condition, letting users bypass password confirmation entirely.

### Files Modified (3 files, 4 locations)

**1. `app/src/main/java/com/beemdevelopment/aegis/helpers/EditTextHelper.java`**
- Added `setEditTextChars(EditText text, char[] chars)` helper method to restore text after it's been cleared by `setEnabled(false)`.

**2. `app/src/main/java/com/beemdevelopment/aegis/ui/slides/CustomAuthenticatedSlide.java`** (first-time setup wizard)
- **Checkbox listener**: Save confirm field text *before* `setEnabled(false)` and restore it *after* — so the text persists across enable/disable cycles.
- **`isPolicyRespected()`**: Removed `|| _checkPasswordVisibility.isChecked()` — passwords must now always match.
- **`onUserIllegallyRequestedNextPage()`**: Removed `&& !_checkPasswordVisibility.isChecked()` — the error is always shown when passwords don't match.

**3. `app/src/main/java/com/beemdevelopment/aegis/ui/Dialogs.java`** (set password dialog)
- **Checkbox listener**: Same save/restore pattern for the confirm field text.
- **OK button handler**: Removed `&& !switchToggleVisibility.isChecked()` — always validate password equality.
- **TextWatcher**: Removed `|| switchToggleVisibility.isChecked()` — OK button only enables when passwords actually match.

### How it works now
When "show password" is checked, the user can see both password fields as plain text. The confirmation field's content is preserved (no longer lost to `setEnabled(false)`), and the equality check always requires both fields to match — regardless of the checkbox state.
